definitions.explanation: A day on which newspapers are not published or delivered. In Japan, all major newspapers observe the same rest days, typically one day per month.

examples.japanese: ⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{休刊日|きゅうかんび}だ。
{休刊日|きゅうかんび}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{新聞|しんぶん}→新聞：01440_shinbun⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{届|とど}かない→届く：00899_todoku⟧。
examples.english: The newspaper doesn't come on no-publication days.

examples.japanese: ⟦{日本|にほん}→日本：03876_nihon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{新聞|しんぶん}→新聞：01440_shinbun⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{休刊日|きゅうかんび}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{月|つき}→月：02230_tsuki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{一回|いっかい}→一回：08925_ikkai⟧⟦あり→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦{各社|かくしゃ}→各社：11057_kakusha⟧⟦{一斉|いっせい}→一斉：01726_issei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{休|やす}む→休む：00606_yasumu⟧。
examples.english: Japanese newspapers have one no-publication day per month, and all companies take the same day off.

notes:
A compound of ⟦{休刊|きゅうかん}→休刊：21658_kyuukan⟧ (suspension of publication) and {日|び} (day). Refers specifically to the coordinated days when newspapers are not published.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{新聞|しんぶん}→新聞：01440_shinbun⟧{休刊日|きゅうかんび}: newspaper holiday
- {休刊日|きゅうかんび}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{当|あ}たる→当たる：01860_ataru⟧: to fall on a no-publication day

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, major newspapers coordinate their rest days so that all papers take the same day off, usually once a month. These are often the day after national holidays or during the New Year period. This practice is unique to Japan and reflects the newspaper industry's labor agreements.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{休刊|きゅうかん}→休刊：21658_kyuukan⟧: suspension of publication — can also mean a magazine ceasing publication entirely
- ⟦{休業日|きゅうぎょうび}→休業日：21152_kyuugyoubi⟧: business holiday — a day when a business is closed
